answer:
What I did: I looked up your recent transactions and the dispute windows in our tariff/docs.

What I found: the charge in question is TX-0401 — amount EUR 240.00 — reason code: service_not_rendered. The transaction date is 2026-07-20. Per our rules the service_not_rendered filing window is 90 days from the transaction date, so the deadline to raise a dispute for this charge was 2026-10-18. That deadline has passed, therefore we cannot open a dispute for TX-0401 today.

What happens next / options:
- Contact the merchant (TechMart Online) and request a refund or reshipment — keep copies of your order confirmation, tracking info (if any), and any messages; these are the best evidence for them.
- If you’d like, I can send a statement for your ACC-1005 account to the email on file showing this transaction (I will not open a dispute). Tell me if you want that and which period.
- If you want further review or escalation beyond these options, I can escalate to a human agent for additional assistance.

I will not open a dispute unless you explicitly ask me to. Which of the above would you like me to do next?

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Limit operations
## Window definition
Limits are tracked on calendar days, not business days. The daily window runs
from 00:00 to 23:59 CET.

Glossary
## Chargeback window
The number of days, counted from the transaction date, during which a dispute
may be raised under a given reason code.

Dispute handling process
## Review timelines
The review target is 10 business days for card reason codes and 20 business
days for transfer reason codes. Complex cases involving a foreign acquirer may
run to 45 calendar days; the customer is notified when that happens.
